newsitem.title: USA: Many consumers confused by mortgage process - survey.
newsitem.headline: Many consumers confused by mortgage process - survey.

text.p: Getting a mortgage to purchase a home or refinance an older loan can be a harrowing and confusing process, according to a survey released Tuesday by the Mortgage Bankers Association.
In the survey of 500 people who had obtained a new mortgage in the last year, about 40 percent of consumers reported being confused by the lending process, the association said.
Confused consumers made a number of suggestions, including that documents be written in plain English, that the overall process be simplified and that all fees be fully explained.

Some consumers also complained of unexpected payments required to get a mortgage. About 28 percent of the survey respondents said they encountered unanticipated fees, most commonly charges directly associated with the loan such as appraisal or loan application fees.

Confused consumers also expressed lower levels of satisfaction with the loan process. About 56 percent said they were extremely or very satisfied compared to 68 percent expressing high levels of satisfaction in the overall group.

The association said it designed the survey, conducted by Yankelovich Partners in early February, with input from the Federal Reserve, Department of Housing and Urban Development, and Consumers Union.
